also: now you know what I mean
I made up my mind not to

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.11: nōbīs erat in animō Cicerōnem ad Caesarem mittere
Liv. praef. 6: ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est
Traupman p. 103: I made up my mind not to hurry, erat in animō nihil festīnāre
terms.comment: Also mihi in animō est, with an infinitive.

evidence: Ter. Ph. 19: Hic respondēre voluit, nōn lacessere.
Ter. Eun. 797: Quid tu tibi vīs?
Traupman p. 103: what do you mean?, quid tibi vīs?
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to intend, purpose, mean”. “I meant to” is often simply volēbam; Quid tibi vīs?, “What do you mean (by this)? What are you after?”.

evidence: Cato, Agr. 1.1: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to have something in mind, to intend, meditate, design, plan”.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.27: an cōnsultō et cōgitātā fīat injūria
terms.comment: Nōn cōnsultō fēcī: I didn’t mean to.

evidence: Ter. Hec. 880: fēcī imprūdēns quam sciēns
terms.comment: Agrees with the subject: imprūdēns fēcī, I did it without meaning to.

terms.gloss: with the best intentions, meaning well
terms.grammar: ablative of quality or manner; Traupman: optimō animō ūtēns
evidence: Cic. Phil. 3.2: sunt enim optimō animō, summō cōnsiliō, of the best disposition (Lewis & Short), s.v. bonus

terms.gloss: how so? how do you mean?
terms.grammar: quī, the old ablative, “how?”, with istuc, “that (of yours)”
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 2.3.10: Quī istuc? Quae rēs tē sollicitat autem? (Lewis & Short s.v. autem)
Traupman p. 103: how do you mean that?, quī istuc vīs?
terms.comment: Asks how what the other person has just said can be so. Traupman adds vīs; the comic poets ask with the bare Quī istuc?.

phrases.latin: ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est
phrases.english: I don’t mean either to vouch for these stories or to refute them.
He meant to answer, not to provoke.
What do you mean by it?

phrases.latin: Erat mihi in animō rēctā proficīscī domum.
phrases.english: I intended to set out straight for home.
Do you mean me? — Yes, you.
Now you know what I mean.
